title: Knowledge check: Deployment Platforms and Containers

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Deployment Platforms and Containers”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Deployment platform concepts” under lesson 226, “Deployment Platforms and Containers”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for deployment and production operations.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Deployment Platforms and Containers”?
options: Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Deployment Platforms and Containers” in a real application?
options: Use a client-submitted user ID as the sole authorization check.
Enforce authorization and data scope on the server for every protected operation.
Hide the link in HTML and trust that users cannot call the URL directly.
Treat a login session as proof of permission to access every object.
questions.answer_key: Enforce authorization and data scope on the server for every protected operation.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Deployment and Production Operations. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
